newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal talks to France Telecom on phone deal.
newsitem.headline: Senegal talks to France Telecom on phone deal.

text.p: Senegal will soon start formal talks with France Telecom on the sale of a one-third stake in telecommunications company SONATEL, according to the head of the state privatisation committee.
The move follows cancellation on April 16 of a provisional deal worth 70 billion CFA ($120 million) with a consortium led by Swedish company Telia Overseas.

"It was clearly stated in the specifications that the period of concession was 20 years for the strategic partner, but Telia wanted a concession of seven years only," Serigne Ahmadou Kamara told Reuters on Friday.
France Telecom made the second best offer, of 65 billion CFA. "We have already had contacts with representatives of France Telecom. I think we will soon start talks with the French," Kamara said.
The Swedish-led consortium wanted a seven-year concession which would have lasted only until the proposed end of the monopoly over the fixed-line network.
"We have the feeling that Telia wanted, after the seven-year period of maximum profit drained from the monopoly of the fixed-phone network, to sell its shares," Kamara said.
Telia's representatives were not available for comment.

The Swedish-led consortium which struck the provisional deal last November also included the Walter Group of the United States, China Telecommunication Services and private Senegalese company Senecom Partners.
Senegal proposes selling the remaining two thirds of SONATEL to private Senegalese and African investors, with 10 percent allocated to SONATEL staff.
Senegal plans to liberalise its cellular telephone sector next year, with January as the target date for the start of a second network.
SONATEL started the West African country's first cellular telephone service in October, using a GSM system.
The state telephone company has a capital of 50 billion CFA francs and an annual turnover of more than 60 billion CFA francs.
